searches.reason: Explore a representation change beyond recency pooling: candidate-conditioned multiple interests grounded in item titles and descriptions, with text representations trained only on the supplied catalog. This could distinguish narrow preferences from broad associations. Seek lightweight methods and ablations separating content grounding from additional model capacity; no external pretrained weights are permitted.

searches.reason: Challenge the assumption that recent interest always implies continued demand. Seek temporal models that distinguish recurring consumption from transitions toward complementary items using training histories, timestamps, and available text. Treat need satisfaction and compatibility as unobserved hypotheses; assess whether learned transition patterns improve ranking beyond simple recency and item-frequency controls.

searches.reason: Investigate whether the main bottleneck is the training objective rather than history aggregation. Compare multi-negative cross-entropy with principled negative sampling and representation regularization, especially for Electronics. Seek methods that address false negatives and popularity effects without assuming that embedding alignment proves collapse; require gains on fixed macro validation HR@10 within the shared GPU budget.
